title: Delinquent day-count 31 from overdue-since 2026-08-01 to business date 2026-09-01 (loan 2)
_note: Parity vector transcribing one non-zero row of the delinquency block read back for SEED-L02 at business date 2026-09-01 under tenant gerege. request.delinquency carries the observed overdue-since civil date 2026-08-01 and the pinned business date 2026-09-01; expect.overdue_days and expect.delinquent_days are TRANSCRIPTIONS of the read-back's delinquent.pastDueDays and delinquent.delinquentDays, both 31. This is the AUGUST row: 2026-08-01 -> 2026-09-01 spans August (31) = 31, a single 31-day month. A 30-day-month approximation reads 30 here and disagrees by 1. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT GRADE: every observed row has delinquencyPausePeriods empty and delinquentDays == pastDueDays, so paused/grace are both 0 and a port that ignores the subtraction passes; no observed overdue date is after the business date, so the negative clamp in OverdueDays is not exercised either. A capture of a loan with a pause period or a grace setting would be needed. TIME ZONE: the request carries bare calendar dates; loan.OverdueDays resolves them through dateOnly [delinquency.go:96,123], which takes the year/month/day IN THE VALUE'S OWN LOCATION and re-anchors to UTC midnight before subtracting, so no offset is hard-coded. These rows are midnight-aligned first-of-month civil dates, so they cannot discriminate a UTC-vs-Asia/Ulaanbaatar parse defect; the day difference between two civil dates is zone-independent.

provenance.note: request.delinquency and both expected cells are transcribed from the committed SEED-L02 loan detail read-back loan-2-detail-raw.json. The overdue-since date is the top-level summary.overdueSinceDate array [2026,8,1] -> "2026-08-01"; the expected cells are the delinquent.pastDueDays 31 and delinquent.delinquentDays 31 in the same file (delinquent.pastDueDate and delinquent.delinquentDate are both [2026,8,1]). The business date 2026-09-01 is the corpus BUSINESS_DATE pinned separately in the seed businessdate capture, cited below. The capture is a single-line JSON document (wc -l = 0), so every observation is at line 1. No value was synthesised: the date and both counts are read directly from the file.
provenance.citation: loan-2-detail-raw.json:1 (single-line committed read-back, tenant gerege): summary.overdueSinceDate [2026,8,1] and delinquent {"pastDueDays":31,"pastDueDate":[2026,8,1],...,"delinquentDays":31,"delinquentDate":[2026,8,1],...,"delinquencyPausePeriods":[]}. Business date 2026-09-01: .softhouse/capture/seed/out/businessdate-get-raw.json:1 "type":"BUSINESS_DATE","date":[2026,9,1]. Arithmetic: 2026-08-01 -> 2026-09-01 = 31 (August).
